PullRequest.Title: Engineering - give the Publish job 300 minutes, so a slow build or ESRP release doesn't cancel it
PullRequest.Body:
The `Publish Build` job starts with the product build and waits for every stage, then for ESRP to finish releasing what's left. Its 180-minute timeout cancelled it in 5 official builds: 475409, 477162, 493716, 494671 and 500111. Each needed a manual rerun of Publish, and the last one released the Thu Nov 19 17:00 UTC insider 7.5 h late ([500111](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=500111)).

The 180 minutes run out in two ways:
- **Waiting for stages.** In 494671, a Linux X64 stage was still in progress when Publish was cancelled.
- **Slow ESRP releases.** In 500111, every stage had finished by 23:30, but ESRP held 5 darwin releases for 50 min until the cancel at 00:20.

## Change

Raise the timeout to 300 minutes:
- First-try successful Publish jobs since Oct 20: p50 102 min, p95 144 min, max 153 min (n=31). So 180 leaves little headroom, and 300 covers a slow build plus a slow ESRP release.
- macOS Sign and Universal jobs alone may take up to 240 minutes (`timeoutInMinutes: 240`).
- The `1es-windows-2022-x64` pool that Publish uses already runs jobs of up to 370 minutes (`product-smoke-flaky`).

**Cost:** Publish holds a Windows agent for up to 2 more hours when a build runs long. It mostly polls while it waits, and it ends as soon as every stage has completed and the releases finish. So the longer cap only matters when the build itself, or ESRP, is slow.

## Validation

- An ADO preview of pipeline 111 on this branch with `VSCODE_PUBLISH` expands `PublishBuild` with `timeoutInMinutes: 300`.
- I haven't queued a publishing run, since Publish only runs in publishing builds and a branch build would publish. The change is a single job setting.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal publishing build completing within the previous 180-minute cap
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Publish starts alongside build stages (dependsOn: []). Job setup, artifact availability and gating tests, serialized downloads/extraction, concurrent artifact publishing, and the final worker join must complete before Publish succeeds. Scheduled releaseBuild and dependent Release/SanityTests follow publishing. Raising the cap does not delay successful completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout/setup, dependency installation, and Node/PowerShell build, authentication, publishing and optional release commands
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One setup sequence and one invocation of each enabled command per attempt; Process artifacts retains its existing retryCountOnTaskFailure: 3.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical commands, ordering and retries with a 180-minute overall deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setup and commands run before job completion; optional release runs only after publishing succeeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve secrets and acquire Cosmos/Blob access tokens
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Fixed setup tasks and two sequential token acquisitions per attempt, independent of artifact count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch build timeline and artifact inventory; download eligible artifact archives
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two inventory requests per polling round, plus normally one archive download per distinct unprocessed eligible artifact. Transient failures retain existing bounded retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same requests, grouping, polling cadence and download serialization for jobs completing within 180 minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Inventory requests and serialized archive downloads/extraction precede worker scheduling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore/write completion state, write/extract archives, read artifacts for hashes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: State initialization once per attempt, append once per successful artifact, archive/extraction and streamed hashing proportional to unprocessed artifact bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical filesystem operations and retained files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Archive preparation blocks scheduling of the next artifact; worker hashing precedes asset creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Blob container/lease operations, CDN existence check, cold staging upload and ESRP submission/status/detail requests, staging deletion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per remaining distinct artifact: lease and CDN check; on CDN miss, staging upload and release submission, up to 720 status iterations at five-second intervals, then details and cleanup. Lease acquisition tries up to 360 times; active leases renew every 30 seconds. SDK/request retries may add calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-artifact operations, local bounds and concurrency; none increases for normal jobs under the old cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Artifact worker completion waits for provision and cleanup; the job joins all workers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create build, create each asset, optionally read release configuration and release the build
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One build creation unless saved state suppresses it, one createAsset stored-procedure execution per successfully processed artifact, and one configuration query plus release stored procedure for an eligible unfrozen scheduled release; existing transient retries apply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Build creation precedes processing; asset creation precedes worker completion; release follows publishing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One PublishBuild job per publishing run; A distinct vscode artifacts excluding SBOMs, typically dozens across enabled platforms; S enabled stages. Artifact processing is deduplicated by name.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Windows agent per PublishBuild job. Two inventory requests run concurrently per loop, followed by serialized downloads/extraction and a 10-second sleep. Workers overlap after serial preparation; their number is bounded by distinct eligible artifacts, not polling iterations. Blob leases serialize publishing for the same friendlyFileName, not globally. This scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persisted State restores completed artifact names from the latest available attempt. done, processing and optionalFailures exclude duplicate processing within the job. A CDN existence check avoids ESRP submission for already provisioned artifacts. Timeline/artifact inventories are refreshed each polling cycle rather than cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff changes only timeoutInMinutes and comments; pipeline callers and publish.ts establish unchanged early termination, boundary counts and scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime measurements or external pipeline history were independently available; ordinary-job duration and actual artifact sizes are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: a larger maximum duration does not add work or delay successful jobs that already finish within 180 minutes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Slow upstream build stages or slow ESRP provisioning exceed 180 minutes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Publish waits for enabled stages and gating jobs, prepares available artifacts as they arrive, then joins outstanding release workers. The new deadline permits this existing work to finish until 300 minutes instead of canceling at 180. It does not impose a 300-minute wait on completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain the allocated Windows pipeline agent while existing work is pending
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One agent per PublishBuild job, with the maximum occupancy increased by 120 minutes only for jobs reaching the old deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Job cancellation at 180 minutes released the agent but prevented pending publication from completing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Allows publishing to progress instead of being canceled; possible contention with other jobs depends on pool capacity and build arrival rates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Continue timeline/artifact inventory polling while stages or eligible artifact discovery remain pending
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two requests per round; at the unchanged 10-second sleep, up to approximately 720 extra rounds/1,440 primary requests over the additional two hours when requests are fast and there are no downloads. Retries/request durations reduce rounds and may add attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same polling boundary and cadence, truncated by job cancellation at 180 minutes; the diff extends its permitted lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Continued requests allow discovery of late artifacts and stage completion; the loop exits once stages complete and all artifacts are accounted for.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Finish late artifact uploads, ESRP provisioning/status polling and blob lease renewal/cleanup
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same work per distinct remaining artifact and existing 720-status/360-lease-acquisition iteration bounds; no added release submission for an already scheduled artifact. Some existing work can now continue beyond the old overall deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These same operations were canceled if the overall job reached 180 minutes, even though macOS Sign/Universal jobs independently allow 240 minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pending workers must complete before Publish and dependent release workflows finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download/extract late archives and record newly completed artifacts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Proportional only to newly eligible unprocessed artifact bytes/names, not additional polling rounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same filesystem operations, prevented from continuing after the old cancellation deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation precedes workers and completion state supports future retries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Record late completed assets and optionally release the completed build
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asset operation per remaining successful artifact; eligible scheduled release retains one configuration query and one release operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same calls, but cancellation could prevent reaching them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Late asset registration and final release can now finish after 180 minutes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S enabled stages and A distinct artifacts, plus time spent waiting for upstream stages and remote releases. At most 120 additional minutes of agent occupancy per long-running PublishBuild job; independent builds may each occupy an agent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same two parallel inventory requests per cycle, serial download preparation, overlapping workers, and per-file leases. Timeout extension introduces no new fan-out loop or worker-concurrency setting.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Completed and in-progress artifact names remain excluded from rescheduling. Additional inventory polling does not redownload already processed artifacts. CDN hits still skip ESRP provisioning; remote status is deliberately polled rather than negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the intentional maximum occupancy/polling-lifetime increase and unchanged processing cardinality. No evidence establishes problematic pool saturation or new wasted-work rescheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual long-build frequency, Windows pool capacity/utilization, remote service duration and resulting queue contention are not established. PR narrative is contextual evidence, not independent measurements.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable high-confidence performance bug: the additional bounded agent occupancy and polling are the explicit availability tradeoff. Unchanged early completion and per-operation limits reject speculative claims of increased normal latency or an unbounded concurrency regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publish retry or stage rerun with previously processed artifacts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Download prior completion manifests, restore State, skip completed artifacts, wait for remaining stages/gates, prepare remaining eligible artifacts and join workers. CDN checks protect already provisioned but not yet recorded artifacts. Retry setup remains on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/azure-pipelines/product-publish.yml: Download all artifacts_processed/Create build/Process artifacts steps
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore completion manifests and rerun existing publishing commands
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One manifest-download step per job attempt; build creation is skipped when a completion manifest exists. Existing task retry count remains three.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same resume/setup logic; the lower cap could require a new attempt but the diff does not change retry policy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write completion manifest and prepare only remaining artifacts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Read the latest available manifest once; archive work for R remaining artifacts and append for each newly successful artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same persistent completion cache and per-artifact filtering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restored state avoids work before worker scheduling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inventory polling, remaining downloads, lease/CDN checks and provisioning only on CDN misses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two inventory requests per round, normally R downloads/workers; CDN hits avoid staging upload/submission/status calls, while misses retain existing bounded polling. Completed D names create no workers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same cache-aware boundary counts and serialization; job stopped at 180 minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only remaining work must finish; extended cap allows longer attempts without changing cache effectiveness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register remaining assets using existing stored-procedure semantics
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One primary createAsset execution per successful remaining worker, with existing transient retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical asset-registration behavior, including already-exists responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before each worker is recorded done.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A distinct artifact names, D persisted successful names, and R remaining eligible names. Archive downloads and workers scale with R, not all A on every poll or rerun.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Setup is sequential; inventory requests are paired; remaining downloads/extraction are serial; remaining workers overlap with per-friendlyFileName blob leases. No concurrency increase per attempt from the timeout setting.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Latest available artifacts_processed attempt populates done; current processing names coalesce work within an attempt. Provisioned CDN resources skip new ESRP release submission even when completion state is absent. Existing transient-retry and optional-failure behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: State and main filtering explicitly exclude previously completed/in-flight artifacts, and processArtifact checks CDN availability before ESRP creation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Retry prevalence and partially completed artifact counts are unknown. Avoided reruns and release-delay improvements are not quantified or established as a specific historical performance regression by code alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the diff preserves resumability, deduplication and warm provisioning behavior. It is not classified as an internal learned regression fix without independently proven historical introducing-change causality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the sole performance-review pass against base f26893c248aa2b2ef1f3dba2134d9d1806559186. Inspected the entire one-file inventory and complete diff, both pipeline callers, publishing/gating/retry logic, authentication and database creation/release paths, and upstream macOS timeout settings. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance findings; the change is a bounded, intentional job-timeout tradeoff with unchanged successful-job termination and per-artifact scheduling. Static review only; no independent pool utilization or duration measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
